neighbours.label: A verb of giving or presenting something to a reader ('gives', 'provides', 'presents', 'will give'), most strongly when a document or section is the subject; it sets up 'an overview'/'details'. Quiet when the sentence uses a non-giving verb.
fire: Soil erosion is a growing problem. This study gives a summary of recent field data.
The second chapter presents a short history of the canal and its builders.
Our handbook provides step-by-step instructions for new volunteers.
Each module of the course gives students practical examples to work through.
Below, the appendix presents the full results of the survey in tables.
This website provides information on local bus routes and timetables.
Next week's lecture will give an introduction to marine ecology.
In short, the brochure gives visitors a sense of what the museum offers.
quiet: Soil erosion is a growing problem. This study was funded by the farmers' union.
The second chapter ends with the canal opening in the spring of 1825.
Our handbook was printed in three languages for new volunteers.
Each module of the course lasts two weeks and meets on Mondays.
Below, the appendix was added after the survey had been completed.
This website was redesigned last year by a small local team.
Next week's lecture will be held in the large hall near the library.
In short, the brochure was too long and most visitors ignored it.

predictions: median fire ~0.35 (probes: 'This report gives an overview' 0.49, 'will give readers' 0.41, 'provides detailed' 0.34, 'presents' 0.25); near misses < 0.15 (weather 0.002). Risk: 'gives' fires even off-topic ('gives the mayor a headache' 0.51), so near misses avoid the verb entirely.
notes: Card: peaks on ' gives' x6, ' presents', ' give', and ' a' before 'comprehensive/full list'; the opposite pole suppresses 'overview', 'comprehensive', 'provides'.
